entry.title: AsyncHttpClient: Replay to a different host sends the original host request and credentials to the new host (CVE-2026-107282)
entry.content:
vulnerability · credential-leakage · CVE-2026-107282

AsyncHttpClient (org.asynchttpclient:async-http-client) contains a critical vulnerability where replayed requests to different hosts inadvertently send the original host's credentials and request data to the new host. This occurs through normal documented features including ResponseFilter failover patterns and IOException retry mechanisms, requiring no special attacker capabilities. The vulnerability has not been reported as exploited in the wild. Users should immediately update to a patched version when available; as a temporary mitigation, avoid using automatic replay/failover features that redirect to different hosts.

entry.title: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via Own Property Check Bypass (CVE-2026-106445)
entry.content:
vulnerability · prototype-pollution-rce · CVE-2026-106445

Handlebars JavaScript template engine contains a critical prototype pollution vulnerability (CVE-2026-106445) allowing Remote Code Execution through the Function constructor bypass. When `allowProtoMethodsByDefault: true` is configured, attackers who control template input can inject arbitrary JavaScript by exploiting the `lookupProperty` function's trust of own properties on `Function.prototype.constructor`. This vulnerability is critical severity; immediate patching is required for all affected versions. Upgrade Handlebars to the latest patched version and disable `allowProtoMethodsByDefault` unless explicitly required, or implement strict template input validation.

entry.title: Handlebars: JavaScript Injection via AST Type Confusion in compile (bypass of CVE-2026-33937) (CVE-2026-106446)
entry.content:
vulnerability · code-injection · CVE-2026-106446

Handlebars.compile() and Handlebars.precompile() functions are vulnerable to JavaScript injection via AST type confusion (CVE-2026-106446), bypassing previous mitigation CVE-2026-33937. The vulnerability allows attackers who can supply untrusted AST objects to inject arbitrary JavaScript code because the functions only validate specific node types while leaving others unchecked. This is critical severity and likely exploited given the prior CVE bypass. Update Handlebars to the latest patched version immediately, and avoid passing untrusted objects directly to compile/precompile functions; validate and sanitize all user-supplied AST input.

entry.title: SMTP is the key: BPFDoor and AVERAT hitting the network edge
entry.content:
red-team · c2, persistence, evasion

BPFDoor and AVERAT Linux implants target telecom and network-edge appliances including mail-security gateways, DVRs, and NAS devices in South Korea and Taiwan. BPFDoor is a passive Berkeley Packet Filter-based backdoor that uses kernel-level packet interception with magic-byte triggers (evolved to hide in HTTPS POST requests to evade detection), while AVERAT is a modular implant beaconing via SMTP to blend with legitimate mail traffic and supporting ten concurrent shell sessions, file operations, and dynamic C2 reconfiguration. Both families are actively exploited in the wild; BPFDoor variants use regional process spoofing (SpamSniper in Korea, Oracle/Sniper daemons in telecom infrastructure) and AVERAT infrastructure comprises compromised consumer/SMB appliances in Taiwan acting as operational relays consistent with China-nexus ORB networks. Organizations should hunt for processes with deleted executables (/proc/pid/exe pointing to deleted), monitor outbound SMTP from non-mail services to consumer-grade hosts, detect raw packet sockets and BPF filters on non-packet-capture systems, and restrict management access to edge appliances while preserving process forensics and DNS records; patch end-of-life appliances where possible and segment network-edge devices.

Read more · Source: rapid7

entry.title: vm2: NodeVM nesting guard accepts array-shaped require and permits host RCE (CVE-2026-92935)
entry.content:
vulnerability · rce · CVE-2026-73483, CVE-2026-92935, CVE-2026-92947, CVE-2026-92953, CVE-2026-92954, CVE-2026-92955, CVE-2026-93605

vm2 NodeVM is vulnerable to a nesting guard bypass (CVE-2026-92935) where passing an array for the require parameter bypasses type checking, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code on the host system with critical severity. The vulnerability affects versions of vm2 where `typeof requireOpts === 'object'` accepts arrays, which then destructure to undefined and permit nesting execution. This is exploitable in the wild when downstream NodeVM instances are configured with `nesting: true` and untrusted code execution. Patch immediately by updating vm2 to a patched version and add strict type validation for require configuration parameters.

entry.title: vm2: NodeVM node:-prefixed negative builtin deny bypass exposes child_process (CVE-2026-92957)
entry.content:
vulnerability · sandbox-bypass · CVE-2026-92957

The npm vm2 package (NodeVM) contains a critical sandbox escape vulnerability (CVE-2026-92957) where negative builtin denials fail to block `node:`-prefixed module specifiers, allowing sandboxed code to require child_process and execute arbitrary processes despite explicit deny policies. This affects configurations using wildcard builtin policies with negative entries like `['*', '-node:child_process']`. The vulnerability is critical severity and likely exploitable in active deployments using vm2 for code sandboxing. Users should immediately update to a patched version once released or implement external process isolation controls as a mitigation.

An attacker can request colliding package names like `evil-left-pad` when only `left-pad` is whitelisted, exploiting non-exact string matching in the allowlist check to load malicious host packages. No indication of active exploitation in the wild is provided. Immediately upgrade vm2 to a patched version; if immediate patching is unavailable, review and remove reliance on external allowlists with custom resolvers as a mitigation.

entry.title: PyJWT: Asymmetric-PEM detection bypass: whitespace/line-ending-mutated public keys skip the HS/asymmetric confusion guard (CVE-2026-102268)
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass · CVE-2026-102268

PyJWT versions prior to patching are vulnerable to asymmetric-HMAC confusion attacks when decoding JWT tokens if the allow-list contains both HMAC and asymmetric algorithms (CVE-2026-102268, critical severity). The vulnerability exploits a bypass in PyJWT's PEM format detection where whitespace or line-ending mutations in public keys cause the `is_pem_format` regex to fail, allowing an attacker with a valid HMAC secret to forge tokens that pass asymmetric signature verification. This impacts deployments mixing algorithm types in the decode allow-list and passing PEM keys as raw bytes/text. Immediately update PyJWT to the patched version and audit configurations to follow RFC 8725 best practices by using single asymmetric algorithms in decode allow-lists rather than mixing HS/asymmetric options.

Upgrade to OpenBao v2.6.0 or later immediately, and consider disabling recovery mode when not actively needed.

entry.content:

TASK#STOMP is a PowerShell backdoor deployed in active campaigns that harvests business documents, Wi-Fi credentials, clipboard data, and screenshots from compromised systems with real-time filesystem monitoring capabilities. The malware represents a significant threat due to its multi-faceted data exfiltration capabilities targeting sensitive business and authentication information. Organizations should implement application whitelisting for PowerShell, enforce execution policies, monitor for suspicious PowerShell activity, and educate users on phishing vectors likely used for initial compromise; apply patches for any identified delivery mechanisms and consider blocking PowerShell execution in environments where it is not operationally necessary.
